title: Cocartesian lifts of base equivalences are equivalences
statement: Use quasicategories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Work in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $E,B$ be small quasicategories and $p:E\to B$ an inner fibration. If $u:x\to y$ is a $p$-cocartesian edge and $p(u)$ is an equivalence in $B$, then $u$ is an equivalence in $E$. Consequently every cocartesian fibration between quasicategories is an isofibration: every equivalence $p(x)\to b$ has an equivalence lift with source $x$. No existence of other cocartesian lifts is required for the first assertion.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 2.4.1.5, dualized to cocartesian edges; Proposition 2.4.4.3 supplies the alternative mapping-space proof recorded in report.md. Read online; WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $z\in E$. Put $A=\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)$, $C=\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)$, $U=\operatorname{Map}_B(p(y),p(z))$, and $V=\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x),p(z))$. These are Kan complexes by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Write $a:A\to C$ for precomposition by $u$, $k:U\to V$ for precomposition by $p(u)$, and $r:C\to V$ for the map induced by $p$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to the given inner fibration and the single horn-cocartesian edge $u$: the resulting square has a weak homotopy equivalence $A\to P(k,r)$ as its comparison map, where $P(k,r)=U\times_{V,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,V)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,V}C$. Its projection to $C$ is $a$. No other lift has been chosen.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite-category dual, as an alternative proof of the forward implication of Proposition 2.4.1.5.

proof.text: Choose an inverse edge $v:p(y)\to p(x)$ of $p(u)$, with its two inverse triangles. By the associative and unital composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], precomposition by $v$ is a homotopy inverse of $k$: the composites are precomposition by $v\circ p(u)$ and by $p(u)\circ v$, respectively, and the triangles identify these with identity classes. Thus for every Kan complex $W$, precomposition by $k$ is a bijection on $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(-,W)$: an inverse is induced by its homotopy inverse, since precomposing a simplicial homotopy with a map to $W$ gives an edge between the resulting maps. The Kan-target testing criterion [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence] therefore says that $k$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This deduction uses only composition and the testing criterion, and does not replace the horn-cocartesian hypothesis by a property of the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Propositions 4.6.8.11 and 4.6.8.12 (unitality and associativity); Notation 4.6.8.15 (precomposition). Kan-target criterion: Kerodon Corollary 3.6.4.3 (03X7).

proof.text: Compare the two cospans $U\xrightarrow{k}V\xleftarrow{r}C$ and $V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}V\xleftarrow{r}C$ by the three maps $(k,\mathrm{id}_V,\mathrm{id}_C)$. These commute strictly and are weak homotopy equivalences. By [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] they induce a weak homotopy equivalence $F:P(k,r)\to P(\mathrm{id}_V,r)$; explicitly $F(t,\gamma,c)=(k(t),\gamma,c)$. The constant-path map $j:C=V\times_V C\to P(\mathrm{id}_V,r)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], since $\mathrm{id}_V$ lifts every horn. Projection $q:P(\mathrm{id}_V,r)\to C$ satisfies $qj=\mathrm{id}_C$, so $q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by two-out-of-three. Composing the weak equivalences $A\to P(k,r)\xrightarrow{F}P(\mathrm{id}_V,r)\xrightarrow{q}C$ proves that $a$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Two-out-of-three here follows directly on components and all based homotopy groups. All path spaces are Kan by the cited comparison statement; neither $r$ nor $p$ has been assumed to be an isofibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9 (invariance), specialized to the three displayed maps, and Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329), specialized to an identity leg. The displayed application is agent-written.

proof.text: The components comparison in [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] turns Step 3 into bijections $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)$ for every $z$. Work in the ordinary category $hE$ provided by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. At $z=x$, surjectivity gives a class $[w]:y\to x$ with $[w][u]=1_x$; it has an edge representative $w$. At $z=y$, the classes $[u][w]$ and $1_y$ have the same image under precomposition by $[u]$, since $([u][w])[u]=[u]([w][u])=[u]=1_y[u]$. Injectivity gives $[u][w]=1_y$. Thus $[u]$ is invertible. The same composition node identifies invertibility of its component class with the two inverse-triangle witnesses defining an equivalence edge, so $u$ is an equivalence in $E$. The inverse construction and cancellation are elementary ordinary-category calculations; the cited nodes supply the component comparison and its interpretation as equivalence edges.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.14 (homotopy category), Notation 4.6.8.15, and the inverse-triangle interpretation of Definition 1.4.6.1. The explicit two-object cancellation argument is agent-written.

proof.text: Now assume that $p:E\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration. For a vertex $x$ and an equivalence edge $\alpha:p(x)\to b$, the existence clause in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a $p$-cocartesian edge $\widetilde\alpha:x\to y$ with $p(\widetilde\alpha)=\alpha$, hence $p(y)=b$ exactly. Steps 1-4 applied to this edge make $\widetilde\alpha$ an equivalence. The same definition already supplies that $p$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories. These are exactly the inner-fibration and source-fixed equivalence-lifting clauses of isofibration in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. The first assertion used only the specified cocartesian edge; existence of lifts is used only in this final consequence.

The statement is unchanged and is the cocartesian dual of HTT Prop. 2.4.1.5. HTT and Kerodon are not in literature/: the report lists them as WANTED and the proof is marked agent-written, which is the correct handling. Step 1: the cocartesian-mapping-criterion ('only if' direction, for one horn-cocartesian edge of an inner fibration) and pinch-comparison (mapping spaces are Kan) give a weak equivalence A->P(k,r) whose C-coordinate is a. Step 2: the inverse v of p(u), with associativity and unitality from mapping-composition, makes precomposition by v a homotopy inverse of k; the Kan-target test (lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence (ii)=>(i)) then makes k a weak equivalence. Step 3: pullback-invariance applies to (k,id,id), and both commutations hold strictly. Path-comparison applies with the identity leg, so j:C->P(id_V,r) is a weak equivalence, qj=id, and two-out-of-three gives q. The composite is exactly a. Step 4: the components clause of kan-realization-serre gives bijections on pi_0. At z=x and z=y these give a two-sided inverse in hE, and mapping-composition identifies an invertible class with an equivalence edge. Step 5: the existence clause of def-coef-infinity-fibrations gives a lift with fixed source, and isofibration is used only through its definition clause. Small cases: B a point; N([1])->pt, where the non-identity edge is not cocartesian, so that hypothesis is needed; a point inside a contractible groupoid, which is not an isofibration; E empty. There is no cycle. No duplicate: the closest nodes are marked-cocartesian-lifting, inert-marked-restriction-fibration and left-cone-restriction-cocartesian. The Mathlib candidate IsStronglyCocartesian.isIso_of_base_isIso is for ordinary categories, so the no-leaf verdict is right. All proof dependencies are in the item's unit except lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence (sk-prop-sf-cbc). I accept that declared tool use: it is a generic black-box test, and lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance already uses it the same way.
